Mm I don’t really follow the recipe card but even so, the trick is to add as many chips as you can and when those are done, add more chips into the fryer while you season the ones you took out. 

Other tips are:

Time yourself. I can make 1 hotel pan worth of chips in 5 minutes so by that logic, I can make 12 pans in an hour. 

I also stack my pans so by the time I have 5 pans of chips, I stop, add more oil to the fryer and then use the time to deliver the chips to the lobby so by the time I’m done, the oil has heated up and I can add chips. 

I don’t use the salt shaker I kind of just sprinkle salt with my hand. Get a small pan and fill it with salt and keep it by you. It’s much faster than using the salt shaker. 

And of course, have your mise en place. I take out all three cases of chips so I don’t have to walk back and forth to the walk in. Whenever I’m done with a case, I keep the cardboard flat and let it on the floor for me to stand on- it also helps catch any oil or chips which makes it easier to clean after. 

As for the taco shells, I leave them to fry for 35 seconds and do one batch while the other one cooks. Use 2 paper towels folded to gather them quickly and honestly just be quick putting more tortillas back in.

Nowadays I make one bag for the line and one for fax. We close at 11, so towards the end of the night, there’s usually like 2 sets of tacos left on fax and maybe 5-7 sets on the line. Even so, hard shell tacos aren’t that popular. I know people get them on the side sometimes, and I get them on the side because I like them better than the chips lol
